anti_generic_signature_read: Removing the shell reveals an apparently elastic-driven wheeled mechanism; the sequence suggests an exposed preparation state followed by assembled travel. Exact winding and release operation remains visually ambiguous.
blind_action_read: Signature image shows two raised-shell states and one assembled car. Six chronological samples of the 16-frame GIF show the shell raised in early frames, internal line configuration changing slightly, then the shell seated and the complete car changing screen position. Animation alone does not clearly expose wheel rotation, winding input or causal powered travel.
blind_form_read: A low wedge-like coupe with faceted roof and hood, broad flat side panels, pointed dark side glazing, wheel cutouts and a flat chassis beneath.
blind_held_read: A small stylized angular gold car toy with black wheels and a removable body shell. No literal hand or size reference is present.
blind_relationship_read: Body shell fits over the chassis; axles cross the chassis and carry wheels. A longitudinal loop runs between an axle-area connection and an opposite chassis anchor.
blind_subjects_read: One car; Four wheels and two transverse axles; Removable gold body shell; Longitudinal loop or elastic-looking line inside the chassis

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Low angular gold coupe body, sloping roof/hood, swept black side glazing and four broad disc wheels. Reference reveal supports this simplified toy interpretation; fine lamp, wheel-face and panel details are not separate Wish requirements.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A toy car with Cybercab reference identity

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Raised shell exposes longitudinal loop connected at the rear axle area and opposite anchor. Blind sequence suggested preparation followed by assembly/travel. After reveal, consecutive frames 0–6 visibly show rear finger/loop movement through winding and return; this resolves the sparse-frame ambiguity without proving physical propulsion.

largest_risk: Quarter-turn elastic operation is represented kinematically; elastic force, traction, loose-loop release and physical travel remain untested. GIF shading stripes reduce polish but do not establish a geometry defect.
resolution: Accept the simplified reference-based toy form and the visible bounded winding/return action. Consecutive initial GIF frames resolve the blind sparse-sampling uncertainty: the rear finger and attached loop change configuration and return before assembled positional travel. No physical-performance inference. Optional presentation improvement: closer exposed-drive framing and higher loop contrast; no geometry repair required by this review. Independently checked metadata-only correction: windows.signature changed from true to false so body is the sole designated signature component. Reversing that one boolean reproduces the previously reviewed concept hash exactly. No form, geometry, function, image or verdict changed; original blind observations and review round 1 remain valid. Independently compared inventory alignment with concept-before-inventory-alignment.json: left/right glazing and the two existing keyed end wheels now have separate component identities and build-group membership; optional traction loops leave the required inventory but remain optional in assumptions. Existing four-wheel form, glazing, elastic winding interaction and physical-verification limits are unchanged. These inventory corrections preserve the visual verdict and round 1; exact image and preflight bindings were rechecked.
